{{Hatnote|For the ''Star Trek'' CCG reboot, see [[Star Trek CCG]].}}
[[File:Skywalker-Ranch-presentation-card-encyc.png|thumb|right|280px|[[Playtest cards#Skywalker Ranch|•Skywalker Ranch]], promotional card made to show Lucasfilm.<ref name="encyc3" /><ref name="bisco20261021" />]]
'''SWCCG 2nd Edition''' was [[Decipher]]'s planned 2001 reboot of [[Star Wars CCG]]. In July 2000 Decipher pitched Lucasfilm a backward-compatible second edition with yearly story-arc environments.<ref name="pres2000" /> Lucasfilm approved none of the program.<ref name="pres2000" /> The license ended on 31 December 2001, so the product was never created.<ref name="ann122801" />

== July 2000 pitch ==

Decipher described 2nd Edition as a product designed to take the best of the present game and expand into new territory.<ref name="pres2000" /> It would bridge to the existing 2,000-card 1st Edition universe.<ref name="pres2000" /> New players would enter without buying 2,000 cards.<ref name="pres2000" /> New players and collectors would be "unencumbered by complexity yet are linked to the successful brand."<ref name="pres2000" />

One game engine would support a broad series of expansions.<ref name="pres2000" /> Each story arc would play in its own self-contained universe.<ref name="pres2000" /> A story arc would be one primary release and two smaller expansion sets in that year.<ref name="pres2000" /> The plan ran for six years of new entry points.<ref name="pres2000" />

Veteran cards would stay "backward compatible with every Star Wars card ever made."<ref name="pres2000" /> Veterans could add the new cards to existing collections and also play a new story-driven environment.<ref name="pres2000" /> Launch was set for the start of the 2001 convention season.<ref name="pres2000" /> The launch would keep the existing tournament structure and add a new league.<ref name="pres2000" />

The same July 2000 presentation also asked for marketing programs and a digital ''Star Wars'' CCG. Lucasfilm approved none of it. See [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]].<ref name="pres2000" />

== If the license had continued ==

Asked what would have happened if the license had continued, Colson said "there would have been a second edition."<ref name="colson-2e" /> He said Decipher did not want one, then would have reached a point where it had to have one.<ref name="colson-2e" /> Later printed Decipher games are the record of that direction after the license ended.

=== One card back ===

Printed SWCCG uses two card backs. Light Side cards carry the Rebel symbol. Dark Side cards carry the Imperial symbol.<ref name="rb20" /> Each constructed deck is 60 cards from one side of the Force.<ref name="rb20" />

Colson said [[Young Jedi]] also used two backs.<ref name="colson-yj" /> He said Republic and Expanded Universe factions would not fit an Imperial or Rebel back.<ref name="colson-back" /> "There were all these pieces in play and motion coming out that were really going to take us down the road to a common back."<ref name="colson-back" /> He said a later reboot would have required one back: "one back, reboot 2.0... It's going to have a single back."<ref name="colson-reboot" />

=== Mixed Light and Dark ===

[[The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game]] (2001) put Free Peoples and Shadow cards in the same draw deck.<ref name="lotr-cr42" /> The draw deck must have at least 60 cards and an equal number of Shadow and Free Peoples cards, shuffled together.<ref name="lotr-cr42" /> Alignment is marked on the face. Free Peoples cards use a light circular field. Shadow cards use a dark diamond.<ref name="lotr-cr42" /> There is one card back for both alignments.<ref name="lotr-back" /> Cultures sit as an icon on the face, not on the back.<ref name="lotr-cr42" />

<gallery widths="180" heights="250">
File:LOTR-card-back.jpg|LOTR TCG card back.
File:LOTR TCG Aragorn Ranger of the North 1R89.jpg|''Aragorn, Ranger of the North'' (2001).
File:LOTR TCG Goblin Runner 1U178.jpg|''Goblin Runner'' (2001).
</gallery>

[[Chuck Kallenbach]] later said Decipher had lived through Star Wars games with "good guy decks and bad guy decks."<ref name="kallenbach-hack" /> For ''.hack//ENEMY'' they used the LOTR system of "good and bad cards in the same deck."<ref name="kallenbach-hack" />

=== Multiple factions ===

[[WARS TCG]] (2004) kept the SWCCG turn, Force piles, location control and battle structure.<ref name="wars-rules" /> It used one common card back for every faction.<ref name="wars-back" /><ref name="colson-wars" /> The five factions are Earther, Gongen, Maverick, Shi and Quay, plus Independent cards that work for any faction.<ref name="wars-rules" /> Color, texture and support icons mark affiliation.<ref name="wars-rules" /> Support icons are a requirement, not a spend.<ref name="wars-rules" />

A constructed deck may include no more than four copies of a single card, except unlimited cards.<ref name="wars-rules" /> Starters were 60 cards, as in SWCCG constructed.<ref name="wars-rules" /> Colson pointed to WARS as the model for a later Star Wars second edition.<ref name="colson-wars" /> He counted three major factions, maybe five in total, and one back.<ref name="colson-wars" />

=== Story-arc environments ===

The 2000 pitch already described yearly self-contained story arcs, so a new player would not need the full 2,000-card pool.<ref name="pres2000" /> Colson said Decipher had also looked at Episode I-only events and formats as a way to move toward blocks.<ref name="colson-blocks" />

=== Star Trek Second Edition ===

Decipher did ship a second edition of [[Star Trek CCG]], first released in 2002.<ref name="wp-stccg" /> Colson said that reboot lost first-edition players.<ref name="colson-lessons" /> He said collectors were about 80% of Trek sales, so the company weathered the drop.<ref name="colson-lessons" /> He called Trek Second Edition more streamlined than First Edition.<ref name="colson-lessons" /> He said Decipher would have used lessons from Star Trek and ''The Lord of the Rings'' in a Star Wars second edition.<ref name="colson-lessons" /> "They didn't get the opportunity."<ref name="colson-lessons" />
